title: Annotatio III §.VII close: Firmiter canon — TRANS SUBSTANTIATIS bread into body; Sagittarius; stop before §.VIII
pass_a_gloss: The Canon of Canonization in the Extravagantes De Fide & summa Trinitate, Firmiter credimus &c., is read in these words: There is one universal Church of the faithful, outside which no one at all is saved. In which Jesus Christ Himself is both priest and sacrifice; His body and blood are truly contained in the Sacrament of the Altar under the species of bread and wine: the bread having been TRANSUBSTANTIATED into body and the wine into blood by divine power, that to perfect the mystery of unity we ourselves may receive of His what He received of ours. And this Sacrament indeed no one can confect unless he be a Priest duly ordained according to the keys of the Church, which Jesus Christ Himself granted to the Apostles and their successors. See also Sagittarius cited above, p. 495 at the end.
pass_b_english: Firmiter (Extravag. De Fide & summa Trinitate): one universal Church; Christ’s body and blood truly under bread and wine species.
Key clause: bread TRANSUBSTANTIATED into body and wine into blood by divine power — only a duly ordained priest may confect (Sagittarius p. 495).
Stop before §.VIII (still on the Scholastic anvil after canonization).
source_text: Canon Canonizationis in Extravag. de Fide & summ. Trinit. Firmiter credimus &c. his verbis legitur: Una verò est fidelium universalis Ecclesia, extra quam nullus omnino salvatur. In qua idem ipse sacerdos & sacrificium Jesus Christus; hujus corpus & sanguis in Sacramento Altaris sub speciebus panis & vini veraciter continentur: TRANSSUBSTANTIATIS pane in corpus & vino in sanguinem, potestate divina, ut ad perficiendum mysterium unitatis accipiamus ipsi de suo, quod ipse accepit de nostro. Et hoc utique Sacramentum nemo potest conficere, nisi Sacerdos fuerit ritè ordinatus secundum claves Ecclesiæ, quas ipse concessit Apostolis & eorum successoribus Jesus Christus. Vide etiam Sagittar. retrò citatum, p. 495. in fin.

lemmas.gloss: bread having been transubstantiated into body
